subject: Science
title: Components of Food
subtitle: Discovering Carbohydrates, Proteins, Fats, and Vitamins that Power Our Bodies!
summary: Food is essential for all living beings. It provides nutrients like carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, and minerals that help our body grow, repair cells, and stay healthy.

sections.heading: 1. What are Nutrients?
sections.content: The major nutrients in our food are named carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, and minerals. In addition, food contains dietary fibres and water which are needed by our body.
sections.pullQuote: Carbohydrates and fats mainly provide energy to our body. Food containing fats and carbohydrates are also called 'energy giving foods'.
sections.digDeeper: Carbohydrates give us quick energy (like sugar and starch in potatoes or rice), while Fats store energy for later (like butter and oils).

sections.heading: 2. Proteins and Growth
sections.content: Proteins are needed for the growth and repair of our body. Foods proteins are often called 'body building foods'. Pulses, milk, fish, meat, and eggs are rich sources of protein.
sections.pullQuote: Growing children need more proteins in their diet than adults because their bones and tissues are constantly expanding!
sections.digDeeper: Pulses (Dal) and paneer are top plant-based proteins loved across Indian households.

sections.heading: 3. Vitamins & Deficiency Diseases
sections.content: Vitamins help in protecting our body against diseases. They also help in keeping our eyes, bones, teeth, and gums healthy. Lack of Vitamin A causes night blindness, while lack of Vitamin C causes Scurvy.
sections.pullQuote: Vitamin D helps our body to use calcium for bones and teeth. Our body also prepares Vitamin D in the presence of sunlight!
sections.digDeeper: Fresh citrus fruits like oranges, lemon, and amla are packed with Vitamin C to boost your immune system.

subject: Math
title: Knowing Our Numbers
subtitle: Unlocking Lakhs, Crores, Place Value, and Comparing Large Numbers!
summary: Numbers help us count objects, compare quantities, and organize information. Understanding the Indian and International Numeral Systems allows us to handle huge numbers easily.

sections.heading: 1. Comparing Numbers
sections.content: To compare two numbers, first check the number of digits. The number with more digits is greater! If digit count is equal, start comparing from the leftmost place value.
sections.pullQuote: 99,999 + 1 = 1,000,000 (One Lakh). Adding 1 to the largest 5-digit number gives the smallest 6-digit number!
sections.digDeeper: In the Indian System of Numeration, we use Lakhs and Crores. Commas are placed after 3 digits from right, then after every 2 digits (e.g., 1,23,45,678).

sections.heading: 2. Estimation and Rounding Off
sections.content: Estimation means finding a number that is close to the exact amount. Rounding off to nearest tens, hundreds, or thousands helps quick mental calculations.
sections.pullQuote: If the digit at the unit place is 5 or more, round UP! If it's less than 5, round DOWN.
sections.digDeeper: For example, 47 rounded to nearest 10 is 50, whereas 42 rounded to nearest 10 is 40.

subject: Science
title: Super Senses
subtitle: How Animals See, Hear, Smell, and Feel the World Around Them!
summary: Animals have amazing senses of sight, hearing, smell, and taste. Ants follow scent trails, eagles spot prey from miles away, and dogs smell hidden objects!

sections.heading: 1. The Power of Smell in Ants & Dogs
sections.content: As ants move, they leave a smell (pheromone) on the ground. The other ants follow the line by smelling their way!
sections.pullQuote: Dogs mark their own area on the road. They can make out if another dog has come into their area by the smell of its urine or stool.
sections.digDeeper: Mosquitoes can find you by the smell of your body, the heat of your body, and the smell of the sole of your feet!
